title: Elodie and the Veil
premise: Cyrus Iversen has survived fifteen years in the magic-outlawed city of Vell by stealing memories and selling them as harmless charms, hiding the truth that she herself is a vessel for a dead god's last prayer. When the old gods stir and begin answering prayers again, the Ministry of Silence hunts every vessel to burn them out—and Cyrus learns her own body is the door through which the vanished country of Elodie can return. Guided by an exiled priest, a memory-thief rival, and the orphan girl she never meant to love, Cyrus must choose between destroying the god inside her to save herself or opening the veil at the cost of her own existence. In the end, she splits the inheritance three ways: the god passes into the girl, Elodie's borders bloom back into being, and Cyrus—half-erased but alive—finally belongs to a family instead of a duty.
about_author: Rosalind Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who inherit burdens they never asked for, from a house full of maps of places that no longer exist.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She sells a stolen first kiss to a grieving widow in Vell's night market, establishing her rules: small memories only, no names, no magic. But the widow's prayer to a forgotten god is answered with candlelight—the first answered prayer in fifteen years. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine; the world Cyrus has carefully made invisible begins to notice her.

chapters.title: What the Ministry Burns
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Ministry of Silence agents raid the market, burning vessels of the old gods alive in the square. Cyrus recognizes one victim as a fellow charm seller and realizes vessels are being hunted systematically. She flees with an orphan pickpocket, Wren, clinging to her coat. Emotional beat: terror and guilt; invisibility has failed, and now someone depends on her.

chapters.title: The Priest Without a God
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with Wren present. Seeking shelter, they find Anselm, an exiled priest who tends a shrine to Elodie, the country erased from maps a generation ago. He tells Cyrus the gods are returning through vessels—and that her stolen memories hide something she's never examined: her own childhood. Emotional beat: reluctant hope; the past becomes a place she might visit.

chapters.title: Memories I Never Stole
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus opens her own hoarded charms and finds memories she cannot remember taking—a border village, a mother singing in a language outlawed, a god's voice asking a child for refuge. She understands she is Elodie's vessel, its last living door. Emotional beat: vertigo and grief; her whole identity was a locked room.

chapters.title: The Rival Thief
chapters.summary: Alternating Cyrus and Sable POVs. Sable, a rival memory-thief who sold Cyrus's name to the Ministry years ago, returns offering help—for a price: the god itself. Their uneasy alliance forms as Ministry hunters close in. Wren begins calling Cyrus 'family,' which terrifies her more than the hunters do. Emotional beat: distrust fraying into fragile loyalty.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The four flee Vell along roads that appear only when prayed over, crossing countryside where Elodie's erased geography flickers through. Anselm teaches them the old rites; Wren shows an uncanny gift for hearing the gods. A hunter ambush costs Anselm his hand. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by cost; the journey is becoming a pilgrimage.

chapters.title: Where Duty Keeps Its House
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the ruined capital of Elodie, the god speaks fully through Cyrus: the veil can be opened, but the vessel dies. Sable urges her to cut the god out and survive; Anselm argues duty demands sacrifice; Wren simply refuses to accept either answer. Cyrus, exhausted, almost chooses erasure just to rest. Emotional beat: the love-versus-duty fracture at its sharpest.

chapters.title: The Price of Doors
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The Ministry arrives in force, led by an Inquisitor who is himself a failed vessel, hollowed and bitter. In the battle at the shrine, Anselm dies holding the veil's threshold open long enough for the others to reach it. Sable betrays them—then, seeing Wren in danger, turns on the Ministry instead. Emotional beat: devastating loss; every easy option burns away.

chapters.title: Three Ways to Split a Soul
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the veil's heart, Cyrus defies the binary choice: she performs a forbidden rite splitting the god's inheritance three ways—one part to Wren, whose gift makes her a living hearth for Elodie; one part back into the land itself; and one part she keeps, half-erasing herself rather than dying wholly. Emotional beat: defiant tenderness; refusing the terms of the sacrifice.

chapters.title: A Country With Her Name On It
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, closing with Cyrus's. Elodie blooms back into being around them—borders, language, shrines—with Wren as its young keeper and Sable staying, unasked and unwelcome and needed. Cyrus, faded but real, watches the first sunrise over a country that exists again, surrounded by the family she built by accident. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging; the door finally opens inward.
